messages.content: Hi there! Thanks for taking the time to chat with me today about the mobile app modernisation project. To start off, could you share what the high-level goals are for modernising the mobile banking app?

Absolutely, I appreciate the opportunity to discuss this. Our main goal with the mobile app modernisation is to really elevate our customer experience and close the gap with some of the fintech competitors out there, like Revolut and N26. 

We're looking to implement real-time notifications for transactions so that customers can stay on top of their spending as it happens. This includes things like seeing the merchant name, the amount, and their remaining balance right away. Another key aspect is enhancing security and ease of use—introducing biometric authentication for logins and giving users the ability to freeze and unfreeze their cards instantly without needing to reach out to us.

We also want to provide valuable insights into spending habits. Automated monthly breakdowns and the ability to set personal budgets would be game-changers for our customers. Plus, integrating features like in-app lending applications and instant payments would really streamline their banking experience.

Of course, we need to ensure that all of this is compliant with PSD2 and GDPR, and we have to work within the constraints of our existing core banking system to avoid making major changes there. Overall, it's about creating a seamless, intuitive experience for our customers while maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance.

Thanks for that detailed overview! It sounds like you have some great goals in mind for the app. Just to clarify, when you mention real-time notifications for transactions, could you explain a bit more about what specific information you want to include in those notifications?

Sure! When we talk about real-time notifications, we're looking to provide our customers with immediate updates on their transactions right after they happen. This means that as soon as a transaction is authorized, we want to send a push notification that includes a few key pieces of information: the amount spent, the name of the merchant, and the customer's remaining balance.

This level of detail not only helps customers track their spending in real time but also adds a layer of security, as they can quickly spot any unauthorized transactions. It's all about giving them more control and visibility into their finances, which is what modern banking should be about in this digital age. 

Additionally, we want to ensure that these notifications are processed and displayed within five seconds of the transaction. Speed is critical here, as we want to create a seamless experience that feels instantaneous.

Got it! So, just to confirm, you want the real-time notifications to include the transaction amount, the merchant name, and the customer's remaining balance, all delivered within five seconds of the transaction. That sounds really helpful for customers. 

Moving on to the security aspect you mentioned, can you tell me a bit more about how you envision the biometric authentication feature working for logins?

Absolutely! For biometric authentication, we want to make logging into the app as secure and convenient as possible. Our vision is to implement both fingerprint and facial recognition technologies. This way, customers can choose the method they prefer for accessing their accounts.

When a user opens the app, they would be prompted to use their device's biometric capabilities—like a fingerprint scan or face recognition—to authenticate themselves. This not only speeds up the login process but also enhances security, as it adds a layer of protection against unauthorized access.

It's essential that this feature is user-friendly and accessible, so we need to ensure it's easy to set up and works seamlessly across a range of devices. By leveraging biometrics, we can significantly reduce the reliance on traditional passwords, which are often a weak point in security. Overall, our goal is to create a frictionless yet secure experience that aligns with modern banking standards.

Thanks for explaining that! So if I understand correctly, you want to implement both fingerprint and facial recognition for biometric authentication, making it easy for customers to choose their preferred method for logging in. You also want to ensure that this feature is user-friendly, accessible on various devices, and enhances security by reducing reliance on passwords. 

Now, regarding the insights into spending habits you mentioned earlier, could you provide more details on what kind of automated monthly breakdowns you would like to offer to customers?

Absolutely! When it comes to automated monthly breakdowns, we want to provide customers with a clear and insightful view of their spending habits. The idea is to categorize their transactions by merchant types, such as groceries, dining, transport, entertainment, and so on. This way, customers can easily see where their money is going each month.

We envision a simple dashboard that presents this information visually, perhaps with charts or graphs to illustrate spending trends over time. For instance, if a customer spent significantly more on dining out one month compared to the previous one, they would be able to spot that trend immediately.

Additionally, we want to include features that allow customers to set personalized monthly budgets for each category and receive alerts as they approach or exceed those budgets. This kind of functionality not only helps users manage their finances better but also encourages more mindful spending. Overall, the goal is to empower our customers with the insights they need to make informed financial decisions.

That sounds really beneficial for your customers! Just to make sure I captured everything, you want to provide automated monthly breakdowns that categorize transactions by types like groceries, dining, transport, and entertainment. You'd also like to include a visual dashboard with charts or graphs to show spending trends and allow customers to set personalized monthly budgets, along with alerts for when they approach or exceed those budgets. 

Lastly, are there any specific limitations or restrictions that you foresee for the app modernisation project?

Yes, there are definitely some important limitations and restrictions we need to keep in mind as we move forward with the app modernization project. 

First, we have to integrate all new features with our existing core banking system through its current API layer. This means we can't make any major changes to the mainframe, which could complicate or delay our timelines. We need to work within that framework to ensure a smooth transition.

Second, we must comply with PSD2 regulations, particularly around strong customer authentication for payment initiations and sensitive account access. This is crucial for maintaining security and trust with our users.

On the data privacy front, all customer financial data needs to be stored and processed within the European Economic Area to comply with GDPR. We're committed to protecting our customers' data, and this is a non-negotiable aspect of our project.

Additionally, any new credit or lending features we introduce will need to align with the Central Bank of Ireland's consumer protection and responsible lending regulations. We want to ensure that we’re adhering to best practices in lending while offering these services.

Lastly, during the transition period, we need to maintain backwards compatibility with the existing app version for at least six months to ensure a smooth user experience and avoid disrupting our customers. Balancing innovation with these constraints will be key to our success in this project.

Thank you for sharing those important constraints! Just to recap, you have several key limitations for the project: 

1. Integrating new features with the existing core banking system through its current APIs without making major changes to the mainframe.
2. Complying with PSD2 regulations, especially regarding strong customer authentication for payments.
3. Ensuring all customer financial data is stored and processed within the European Economic Area to meet GDPR requirements.
4. Aligning any new credit or lending features with the Central Bank of Ireland's regulations on consumer protection and responsible lending.
5. Maintaining backwards compatibility with the existing app version for at least six months during the transition.

I appreciate your insights today! Based on our conversation, I have gathered the following clear requirements:

1. Real-time notifications for transactions including the amount spent, merchant name, and remaining balance, delivered within five seconds.
2. Biometric authentication for logins using fingerprint and facial recognition, ensuring user-friendliness and accessibility across devices.
3. Automated monthly breakdowns categorizing transactions by merchant types, with a visual dashboard and personalized budget-setting features.
4. Compliance with PSD2 regulations, GDPR for data privacy, and Central Bank of Ireland regulations for any new lending features.
5. Integration with the existing core banking system via current APIs and maintaining backwards compatibility with the existing app version for at least six months.
